direction.name: The product performs
direction.idea: Software is most convincing when it is doing its job in front of you. Instead of describing features, put small, true, working fragments of the product on the page: the actual control, with real content, responding to the pointer. A colour picker's loupe reads the page's own background and prints its value. A list tool lets you tick an item right there. A type-scale plugin sets the page's own headings. Find the one interaction that is the product and make the hero that interaction; then show each further capability as another fragment at real size. No dashboard collage, no browser frame, no screenshots shrunk until unreadable.
direction.composition: Hero: a short plain headline (4–6vw, left-aligned, upper-left third) and one sentence; the rest of the first screen is the main fragment at actual interface size, sitting directly on the page or on one flat stage colour, large enough to read every label. The fragment is built in HTML and works. Below, capabilities are a single-column sequence, each a row of two parts on a 5/7 split: a two-line statement on one side and the relevant fragment on the other, with the fragments varying in size and shape so the column never becomes a zigzag of equal blocks. Fragments are cropped pieces of interface (a menu, a row, a control, a panel edge), not whole windows. One section pins a fragment while three short statements change it.
direction.typography: The marketing type matches the product's interface type so the fragments and the page feel like one thing. Headline modest; interface text at its true size (13–15px) inside fragments.
direction.colour: Neutral ground. The product's own interface colours provide the colour. At most one flat stage colour behind fragments.
direction.imagery: The interface fragments are the main imagery: build them carefully with real labels, real numbers and sensible states (one hovered, one selected). Around them, two or three real pictures of the customer's world (found with scripts/assets.mjs), never stock of people at laptops.
direction.richness: Fidelity. A fragment with believable content and a real hover state is more interesting than any illustration. Spend the effort there.
direction.pitfalls: A fake interface made of grey bars and circles is the worst outcome; if you cannot build a believable fragment, change direction. Mark each fragment's root element with the attribute data-ui: inside it the product's own conventions apply (1px control borders, small radii, a shadow on its open menu) and the inspector leaves them alone; outside it the house rules hold as usual. data-ui is for cropped fragments only, never for a page wrapper. Do not put the fragment in a browser or laptop frame.

hero.name: Controls on the sentence
hero.blueprint: A dark flat ground with no logo bar: a 14px wordmark top-left and the single action as an underlined text link top-right, both 28px in. The headline is a two-line sentence, centred, at clamp(96px, 9vw, 150px), line-height 1.0, occupying the middle 64% of the width and sitting slightly above the midline. It is set in a variable font and it is the demonstration. Three small control chips from the product sit on top of the sentence, each about 300 by 80px with the product's true radius, a text label and a numeric readout: one above the first line near its left end, one overlapping the start of the second line, and a two-state switch at the lower right. They are tilted 2 to 4 degrees and filled solid, one step lighter than the ground. Each one works: dragging the first changes the headline's weight through `font-variation-settings`, the second changes its letter-spacing, the third toggles uppercase. Mark each chip's root with data-ui. One supporting sentence at 17px, max 40ch, is centred 72px under the headline. The bottom third of the screen stays empty.
hero.mobile: The sentence stays on two lines at 13.5vw, centred at 38% of the height. The three chips shrink to 200 by 60px and move off the letters: one above the sentence and two side by side beneath it, untilted and still live. The supporting sentence follows at 16px. The wordmark stays top-left and the action link top-right.
hero.headline: A two-line sentence of three to five words, up to about 11 characters per line at 9vw, that still reads when its weight and spacing change.

type.note: A geometric sans in a light weight at large size, soft and exact at once, with its text cut underneath. Suits consumer apps, utilities and developer tools that want to feel calm and modern.

palette.name: Lunar and bronze
palette.note: Soft black holds the page with panels one step lighter, white text and grey secondary lines, so photographs supply all the colour. Muted bronze goes on small markers and the one button only.

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Sentences with switches
sections.blueprint: Four or five capabilities, each one plain sentence of five to eight words about what the product will do for you, each ending in a working switch. Every sentence is a full-bleed band 20vh tall, butted against the next with no gap. Inside, on the 12-column grid: the sentence at clamp(30px, 3.6vw, 60px) on one line in columns 1–10, vertically centred; in columns 11–12, right-aligned, the product's real toggle, built in em with its root marked data-ui, 1.1em tall so it matches the type. Off, a band is the page ground and its sentence is in the soft ink. On, the band fills with a palette colour, a different one per band, the sentence turns to full ink and a second line at 17px appears beneath stating the consequence in figures. Two bands are on at load. Toggles answer click, Space and Enter. There is no heading; the first sentence does that work.
sections.mobile: Bands are at least 132px tall. The sentence is set at 6.4vw on two lines in the left 76% of the width; the toggle sits at the right, vertically centred, with a 44px touch target. When a band is on, the consequence line opens under the sentence at 15px.

sections.name: Pinned fragment, changing state
sections.blueprint: Two columns. Right, columns 7–12: a stage that is position: sticky; top: 14vh, holding one fragment of the real interface at true size on a single flat stage colour, about 520px square. Left, columns 1–5: three statements, each in its own block 80vh tall, so one is in view at a time. A statement is a two-line sentence at 28–32px that begins with its order word ('Paste a link.', 'Then pick the parts you want.', 'Share it when it looks right.') plus one supporting line at 16px. The statement nearest the viewport's centre is in full ink; the others sit at 30%. As each statement becomes active the fragment changes to the matching state: an empty field, a filled list with two rows selected, a finished result with its confirmation. Build the states in HTML and switch a class; do not swap screenshots. The heading, two to four words at 24–28px, sits above the first statement.
sections.mobile: The stage is sticky at the top, 46svh tall, the fragment fitted by cropping to its active region, not by shrinking its text. Statements scroll beneath it in blocks 60svh tall at 22px. The stage releases after the third statement.

sections.name: One quiet logo row
sections.blueprint: Only for real logos supplied by the project; if none are supplied, set the names in the text face at 22px in the same row and never draw stand-ins. The row reads as a sentence: it opens at the left margin with two to four plain words at 18px (the phrase that introduces the names), vertically centred on the logos, and five to seven logos follow on the same line, spread to the right margin with `justify-content: space-between`. Every logo is normalised to one optical height (28–32px for wordmarks, 36px for compact marks) and one colour, the page ink, using single-colour SVGs with `fill: currentColor`. The band is tall and almost empty: 120–150px of ground above and below the row, no box, no background change and no separate heading. Logos stay still; nothing scrolls or fades at the edges.
sections.mobile: The opening words sit alone on the first line at 17px. Logos follow in a grid of two per row, each 26px tall and left-aligned in its cell, with 36px between rows. Show six at most; there is no sideways scrolling.

sections.name: A sentence with a blank
sections.blueprint: The closing sentence has a gap in it, and the gap is the form. A sentence of five to eight words is set at about 6vw on two lines, flush left across columns 1–11; there is no separate heading. Where the reader's email (or name, or city) belongs, an `<input>` sits inline on the baseline: a filled block of the one-step tone, exactly one line-height tall and about 7em wide, with the placeholder in the same face and size in the softer ink, no border, and the page's radius or motif corner. The sentence's last word is the submit `<button>`, set in the same type on a block of the accent colour of the same height. Field and button use `em` units so they scale with the sentence. One line at 16px under the sentence, in the softer ink, says what happens after sending. Nothing else is in the section.
sections.mobile: The sentence is set at 10vw on two lines; the input drops to a line of its own between them at full width and one line-height tall, and the final word, as the button, ends the second line. The explaining line follows at 15px.

references.name: Dabbit
references.idea: The colour picker demonstrates itself on the page: its loupe sits in the hero reading the site's own background hex, and every feature is shown as a real fragment of the app.
references.hero: Near-black viewport split exactly in half by a one-pixel vertical hairline. Left half: a small chrome four-petal logo top-left at a 40px margin, then two thirds of empty dark, then everything else anchored bottom-left: a one-line 30px medium-weight headline, three lines of grey 18px copy, a light pill button beside an outlined pill, and a tiny note. Right half: a 450px rounded square with a thin iridescent border, the app's loupe, empty except for a centre crosshair dot and a small chip reading the hex of the page's own background. Eight pastel dots and lozenges drift across the top-right like spilled swatches.
references.type: InterVariable only. Headline a modest 30px medium with -0.025em tracking; section heads about 22px; cell titles 15px; body 16px grey. Largest text is 3.3vw. Hierarchy comes from white against grey rather than size; hex values use tabular figures.
references.colour: #141416 #2b2b2e #f4f3f2 #9a9aa0 #f4a48c #d4c6e6 — Charcoal ground, off-white and grey text, no brand accent. All colour comes from the product: pastel swatches, tonal scales, and a thin prismatic edge on the loupe and logo. Neutral-cool.
references.imagery: Live-drawn UI fragments on canvas: swatch strips, eleven-step scales, contrast tables, a Figma plugin panel, each in a slightly lighter rounded panel. A chrome 3D logo and chrome price numerals are the only non-UI images.
references.layout: 40px outer margins; the hero's centre hairline becomes a three-column then four-column hairline grid. No section changes background; rhythm is small eyebrow, heading, grid, repeat. Text sits top-left in every cell.

sections.description: A three-column grid ruled by one-pixel hairlines with no card backgrounds. Each cell is over 400px tall: 15px white title and three lines of grey copy, plus a real UI fragment docked above or below (a swatch history strip, a tonal scale, a contrast table, a ten-by-ten colour matrix). Rows alternate text-over-mock and mock-over-text so the grid staggers. The loupe square from the hero reappears floating across cell boundaries.

A four-column, three-row grid of minor features divided by hairlines. Each item is a 14px title prefixed by a tiny coloured glyph (dot, square, triangle or dash, one shape per column, in the app's pastel colours) and two lines of grey text. No icons, no cards, no hover chrome.

Left third: small grey eyebrow, a 22px heading, one paragraph. Right: the price rendered as huge chrome 3D numerals about 150px tall with the loupe square overlapping them, a tiny qualifier beside, and a plain four-line checklist beneath. No pricing card, no border, no tiers.

Closing block centred on the same dark ground: the chrome four-petal logo enlarged to about 200px, pastel shapes scattered widely around it, a two-line 22px sentence, the same two pill buttons, then a one-line footer with copyright left and seven text links right.

steal: Make the hero demo sample the page itself: the tool reports the site's own background value, proving the product without a screenshot.
Build feature grids from hairlines and real UI fragments instead of bordered cards and icons, alternating text-above and mock-above per row.
Keep the headline small (30px) and anchored bottom-left so the product object, not the slogan, owns the first viewport.

references.name: Rows
references.idea: Radical understatement: a product about simple lists is sold with a 27px headline, 12px copy and a column of small live demos, each proving one interaction.
references.hero: Warm off-white page, almost empty. Everything hangs on one vertical line 27% in from the left. A small striped-letter logo mark sits there near the top; 220px lower comes a two-line headline at only 27px (under 2vw), then three lines of 13px body about 370px wide, then a near-black rectangular button with 4px corners beside a text link with an arrow. A single grey sign-in link sits in the top-right corner; there is no navigation bar. More than 80% of the viewport is blank. At the bottom edge the first feature module peeks in: grey demo panel left, short text column right.
references.type: Suisse Intl only, weight 450–500, tracking −0.04em. Headline 27px, feature headings about 16px on two lines, body 12px. Three sizes in total, no uppercase and no display moment; hierarchy comes from weight and empty space alone.
references.colour: #f5f6f1 #e6e7e1 #1a191d #ffffff #c7372f #3aa56a — Warm paper off-white with slightly darker grey-green demo panels and near-black type; colour appears only inside the UI as priority dots, outlined status pills and one green or red action button.
references.imagery: No pictures: small live-rendered fragments of the app (two or three white list rows with dots, status pills, avatars and a visible cursor) sit in flat grey panels of fixed 368px width with barely rounded corners.
references.layout: One content block about 650px wide, offset left of centre, repeated down the page: 368px demo panel plus a 245px text column, top-aligned, separated by 200px or more of empty space. The logo mark sticks to the top-left corner on scroll. Footer is one line.

sections.description: The repeating module: a flat grey panel roughly 368px wide and 120–190px tall holding a tiny mock list (white rows with 6px radius, a coloured numbered dot at left, task title, an outlined status pill, an avatar, a chevron) and often a cursor mid-action. To its right, 20px away and top-aligned, a medium-weight heading of one or two lines and two short paragraphs at 11–12px in a column only 245px wide. Modules never alternate sides; they stack with large gaps.

The closing block keeps the same narrow measure: a three-line paragraph at 13px, then the identical button and arrow-link pair from the hero, left-aligned on the text column's axis. After a long gap a single hairline spans the 650px block and under it sits one row of tiny footer text: brand line at left, six links and a copyright strung along the right.

steal: Set the headline at near-body size (under 2vw) and let empty space, not scale, give it importance.
Explain each feature with a tiny cropped fragment of real UI in a fixed-width flat panel, one interaction per panel, with the cursor left visible.
Hang the whole page on one off-centre left edge and never break it, logo and footer included.

references.name: Juggle
references.idea: The headline literally drowns: a flat blue field rises to half height and the lines below the waterline turn from red to submerged navy.
references.hero: Two flat fields: white above, saturated blue below, meeting at exactly half height. A three-line all-caps headline in a black-weight grotesque at 8.4vw is centred across the seam, about 65% of the width, lines nearly touching. The first line sits on white in red-orange; the second is cut by the seam, and its lower half plus the whole third line render dark navy as if under water. Small red logo top-left, a rectangular red button with tracked caps top-right. Near the bottom, one line of white condensed caps names the audience. No image, no sub-paragraph.
references.type: Acme Gothic Black 900 caps at 122px, -0.03em, for the hero only. Section heads use Helvetica Now Display Condensed bold caps around 48 to 70px; body is Helvetica Now 17px; labels are small tracked caps. Roughly a 7:1 headline-to-body jump.
references.colour: #2e2eff #ffffff #ff3b1f #0a0a0a #f5f3ef #020156 — Three flat poster colours each own whole sections: electric blue, red-orange and black, with white and warm off-white for product areas. No tints, no gradients.
references.imagery: Simplified product UI on a cream rounded panel over black with a small video-call window; otherwise flat vector graphics: a pair of blinking eyes, a smiley cut into shuffled square tiles.
references.layout: Full-bleed colour blocks with one message each, mostly centred. Product sections switch to a two-column split on off-white with about 90px margins. Marquee strips separate blocks and a slim sticky bar carrying the CTA rides the bottom edge.

sections.description: Full-screen electric blue. Centred stack: a tiny tracked caps label, three lines of white condensed bold caps at about 5vw, a gap, then a single heavier, wider word at a larger size as the punchline, a faint blurred line of text beneath it and an outlined rectangular button. Wide empty margins left and right.

Problem check on full-screen red-orange, under a white marquee strip of condensed caps with small red buttons repeating inside it. Centre: a two-line white condensed caps heading at about 5vw; below, a flat illustration of two white almond eyes with black pupils; a tracked caps instruction line; then three evenly spaced white outlined checkboxes, each with a two-line caption, one already ticked.

Black section. A small tracked caps title centred, under it three numbered text tabs in a row with the active one underlined. Below, a cream rounded app window about 55% wide fills the rest of the viewport: mostly blank note area, a floating status chip, and a small dark video-call window with three faces overlapping its lower edge.

White. Left: a narrow column of small body text, two founder names with roles, then three link columns under tracked caps labels. Right: a blue square about 280px holding a white smiley face sliced into a three-by-three grid of tiles that are rotated and shuffled like a sliding puzzle. Tiny logo and copyright bottom-left.

steal: Split the hero into two flat colour fields and recolour the headline where it crosses the seam, so the layout acts out the copy.
Give each section one saturated flat colour and one sentence, and separate them with a thin marquee strip.
Turn a pain-point list into a mock checklist with real checkboxes under a blunt question heading.
